rows.summary: Chaos Mesh experiment ~133 min ago killed all 3 Kafka broker pods; all restarted, but broker `lakehouse-dual-role-0` JMX endpoint is unresponsive — Prometheus cannot scrape it, keeping the KafkaBrokerDown alert firing. 60 partitions remain under-replicated; no offline or under-min-ISR partitions, so writes continue.

Chaos Mesh experiment ~133 min ago knocked all 3 Kafka brokers offline simultaneously; all pods are back Running/Ready, but broker-0's metrics exporter is wedged (not scrapeable), keeping the KafkaBrokerDown alert firing. The cluster is functionally healthy (0 offline partitions, 0 under-min-ISR) but has 60 under-replicated partitions still catching up and no visible active-controller metric (because broker-0, likely the KRaft controller, is not being scraped).

Broker lakehouse-dual-role-0 is Running/Ready in Kubernetes but its Prometheus metrics scrape is failing, causing the alert to count only 2/3 brokers as reachable. All brokers suffered a simultaneous chaos-mesh-induced kill ~129 minutes ago; the other two brokers fully recovered, but broker-0 still shows 60 under-replicated partitions and active_controllers=0 (no KRaft controller visible from scraped metrics). No partitions are offline or below min-ISR, so writes still succeed, but the cluster has zero fault-tolerance margin until broker-0 is healthy.

The Flink taskmanager was forcibly terminated (TaskExecutor shutdown, exit code 255) ~2 minutes ago, causing ~2 in-flight checkpoints to fail and triggering the alert. The job restarted automatically from its last checkpoint and is now RUNNING/STABLE, completing ~25 checkpoints in the last 5 minutes. Chaos Mesh is active and its pattern of repeated deployments correlates with pod terminations.

Flink checkpoint failures were triggered by a task manager pod restart ~2 minutes ago (TaskExecutor shutdown event). The job is already recovering: RUNNING/STABLE with ~25 completed checkpoints in the last 5 minutes. Chaos Mesh deployments active in this window are the likely cause of repeated disruptions.
Flink checkpoint failures were caused by a TaskExecutor shutdown ~2 minutes ago (chaos-mesh fault injection); the job has self-recovered and is completing checkpoints normally. No action needed.

Node lakehouse-worker (zone-a) is unreachable, taking down Kafka broker lakehouse-dual-role-2 (60 under-replicated partitions), the Flink job manager, and the ingestion service pod on that node. Cluster still writes (0 under-min-ISR) but has zero fault-tolerance margin. Human intervention is needed to replace the node.

Node lakehouse-worker (zone-a) is unreachable, taking down Kafka broker lakehouse-dual-role-2 and the Flink JobManager with it. The cluster is degraded (60 under-replicated partitions, consumer lag 300) but still serving writes (min ISR still met). Manual node recovery or replacement is required.

Node lakehouse-worker (zone-a) is unreachable, taking down Kafka broker lakehouse-dual-role-2, the Flink job manager, and one ingestion-service replica. 60 partitions are under-replicated; writes still flow (min ISR=2 met) but there is zero fault-tolerance margin. A chaos-mesh deployment ~160 min ago correlates precisely with the failure.
